title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with funding rounds and strategic partnerships, while the U.S. government continues to bolster its space resilience budget. Meanwhile, launch plans are facing unexpected hurdles, and the AI for Defense trend is gaining traction.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy in Space
themes.body: Iceye's hefty €1 billion raise and Isar Aerospace's €270 million boost highlight a growing appetite for investment in satellite technologies. This influx suggests that the space economy is maturing, but it also raises questions about sustainability in a crowded market.

themes.title: Government Budget Boosts
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion increase for space resilience indicates a clear prioritization of national security in space. This funding could catalyze new initiatives, but it also risks creating a dependency on government contracts for private players.

themes.title: Launch Delays and Challenges
themes.body: New Glenn's recent setbacks have forced NASA to rethink its lunar ambitions, showcasing the fragility of ambitious space plans. As hypersonic tests continue to slip, the industry may need to recalibrate expectations around timelines and technological readiness.

themes.title: AI's Role in Defense
themes.body: The surge in 'AI for Defense' startups reflects a broader trend of integrating advanced technologies into military operations. However, the question remains whether these innovations can deliver on their promises without falling prey to the typical pitfalls of hype.
